title: Simulation under register bounds
statement: Let $R\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\Lambda$ be a finite set of labels, let $P$ be a counter program over $R$ registers with labels in $\Lambda$, choose a start label $\ell_0\in\Lambda$, and let $x$ be an input bit string. For every $B,t\in\mathbb{N}$ and abstract state $s$ with read position at most $|x|$, suppose that for every $j<t$ and every register $r$, the value of register $r$ after $j$ steps of $P$ on $x$ from $s$ is at most $B$. Then there exists $t'\le t(2B+5)$ such that the compiled machine started at $\ell_0$, run on input $x$ from the encoding of $s$, reaches the encoding of the state obtained after $t$ steps of $P$ on $x$ from $s$.
hypotheses_covered: A counter program $P$ over $R$ registers and $\Lambda$
An abstract state $s$ with read position at most $|x|$
For every $j<t$, every register of the state reached after $j$ steps has value at most $B$
